title: Translate a session imported from Claude Code into a Codex 0.156.0 rollout with a loss account beside it
blocked_by: R10 and R11 only: the proof account, a Codex login with room to make requests, logged into a scratch Codex home by the card's lead seat, Archie, with Codex's own login act. It is not the Chippy and Gypsy account, which is at its usage limit until 30 September 2026. No pool file on the proving machine names a Codex role, so none is invented. If no Codex account with room exists when R10 comes up, R10 and R11 are blocked, and the act that unblocks them is a login with room or that account's 30 September reset; no account is borrowed. R1 to R9 build and land on their own evidence without it.
purpose: The home's first translation to another harness, one named pair and one measured version: a session imported from Claude Code is rendered as a rollout in the shape Codex 0.156.0 writes and reads for its own threads, with every text part, tool call and tool result carried whole as Codex's own items, readable thinking carried as text and opaque blocks dropped (P3), and a JSON loss account beside it naming by entry id and hash what was kept, what changed and how, and what was lost and why. It improves on Codex's own importer of Claude Code files, which is a compaction and not a copy, and never adopts or calls it (ADR-022). The Codex thread is a fork of the session, never the same session: it announces itself in band, and its durable link back is the loss account and a side leaf on the session, which a Codex compaction cannot erase.
task: Add a Codex profile beside the Claude Code one, crates/lys-home/src/harness/codex/, and a subcommand `lys-home translate-codex --home H --session S --out DIR --codex-version V --zone Z` in its own crates/lys-home/src/cli_translate.rs (cli.rs is 433 code lines against the 500-line cap, so it gains only the variant and its dispatch). `--out` is a Codex home directory: the rollout is written under it at Codex's own layout, sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-<local date and time>-<thread id>.jsonl, and the loss account beside it. The render walks the session's context path as the Claude Code render does (entry order, then part order), reads no clock, no random source and no network, and derives the thread id as record_uuid of the session head (ADR-016, CN9), so each head makes a new Codex thread. **The Codex thread is a fork of the session and not the same session:** once Codex continues it, its turns never come home. The in-band marker says so, but a Codex compaction can erase it, so the durable link back is the loss account and the lys.translation side leaf the translation hangs beside the context path (ADR-012), which never moves the head, so the Claude Code render of the same session is unchanged by a byte. The item shape is the one measured from rollouts Codex writes on the machine the proof runs on; rollouts written by 0.155 on that machine are the starting point for the tool items, because the only 0.156.0 rollout there holds no tool item, and R10's recording is what decides: if it shows a shape R3 or R4 did not write, R10 corrects the render and every earlier test is run again. Codex's source checkout on the proving machine, older than 0.156.0, is never read as the shape. The Codex account is named by its role, the proof account: a Codex login with room to make requests, logged into a scratch Codex home with Codex's own login act, `CODEX_HOME=<scratch> codex login`. It is not the Chippy and Gypsy account, which is at its usage limit until 30 September 2026, and no other person's account is borrowed. No pool file on the proving machine names a Codex role, and this brief invents none. The scratch Codex home is a directory outside the repository's working tree; the live Codex home is never read, copied or written, every Codex command runs with `CODEX_HOME=<scratch>` on its own command line and the proof records each one, and no step copies auth.json or any credential file (CN8, ADR-001). **R10 and R11 are performed by the card's lead seat, Archie, on the proving machine, in the scratch home, after the chain has built and landed R1 to R9 and the lead has signed the build off.** The chain's builder has no Codex login and never runs them, and the proof records the seat and the date beside its hashes. Before any recording, and before each resume attempt, exactly one request from the scratch home checks that the proof account can make requests; it ends when `codex exec` exits, with no timeout. When it exits non-zero the row refuses with `the proof account in the scratch Codex home cannot make requests: log in there with a Codex account that has room, or wait for its limit to reset`, whose act is that login or that reset. If no Codex account with room exists when R10 comes up, R10 and R11 are blocked and say so in Blocked by. R10's recording, bounded to two attempts, and R11's resume, bounded to three attempts, are the last two rows and the only ones that spend Codex requests; everything before them lands on its own evidence, so the build is not held on the account. The marker carries no template hash: no Codex launch template exists and none takes part, so the marker names the source session id, the source head hash (Session::head_hash at render time) and the Codex version the rollout shape was recorded against, the same three things the account and the side leaf carry, so all three name one thing. The words' phrase "the render's template hash" is read as this source head hash, so no reader looks for a template. `translate` in rollout.rs is the one entry point: R4 writes it, R5 extends it with the carried sidechains, the off-path rows and a forked child's prompt, and R6 extends it with the side leaf, so each row is built on the rows before it. A forked child's carried user message is written after the whole walked history as the thread's next user prompt, as the Claude Code launch line passes the seed after the resumed history. Its text is read through seed_of, which opens the parent session's file (ADR-017), so the translation's read boundary is the session file and, for a child forked at a user message, that parent file, which the translation opens once more to name each non-text part seed_of skips as a lost row. The account measures the entry as the home holds it. The words' block hash is the hash of the entry part as the home entry holds it: the SHA-256 of serde_json::to_vec of the part's JSON value in the entry, the rule the Claude Code render's loss account already uses, and never a stored block. Kept means the Codex item carries that part whole. **The importer drops a tool_use's caller field when it imports the file, and that loss is recorded nowhere yet:** import.rs rebuilds each tool_use as a toolCall holding only type, id, name and arguments, and its ImportReport holds counts only, so no importer account exists and a home toolCall never holds caller. The board 5 card "The importer records every field it drops" carries that fix, and this translation cannot name a field the home entry does not hold. The translation never reads a stored block and has no BlockNotStored refusal, and the one refusal in this subcommand that tells the caller to re-import the source file is the unparsed-stamp refusal of R1. A field the entry itself holds beyond what its Codex item carries is still counted as changed, named `<key> not carried`. A labelled sidechain that descends from the context path is carried as marked text and counted changed (R5); sidechains, harness events, lanterns and other lys entries that are off the path and not carried are lost rows with their kind and a true reason, so the resumed thread sees exactly the subagent traffic the account says it carries. A branch_summary or custom_message on the context path feeds the model's context, so each is carried as marked developer text under its own marker, as the compaction is, and counted changed; off the path, each is a lost row whose reason is that it is off the context path. Every entry of the root-to-head path that a compaction leaves off the context path is a lost row naming that compaction; an imported compaction keeps nothing before it, since its first kept entry is itself, so every entry an imported session holds before its last compaction is such a row, and the descent rule of R5 covers the whole path from root to head. A message of any role but user, assistant and toolResult, a toolCall with no id or no name, and a toolResult with no toolCallId are each a lost row with a named reason; the translation never gives a missing field an empty default. A part a carried sidechain or custom message holds that marked text cannot carry, a base64 image included, is a lost row with its reason. An image part whose source is base64 is carried as Codex's input_image item with no `detail` key, in a user message and inside a tool result alike, and R11 measures that Codex 0.156.0 resumes a thread holding one; an image of any other source is listed lost and never fetched, and the translation reads nothing beyond the session file and a forked child's parent file. **Red first:** each code requirement's named tests (R1 to R7) land in a commit of their own before the commit that adds its implementation, and at that commit the requirement's test command is run and seen failing, exiting 101; R8 and R9 add no implementation of their own, and R10's correction, when its fixture test fails, takes that failing run as its red. The jiff crate is added with its default features off and its tzdb-bundle-always feature on, so the time zone database is the one bundled in the build, the system database is never read, and one zone name gives the same offsets on every machine. The loss account serves S4's written account of what each render or translation lost, and R2 cites it; S4 is split with HOME-001, whose render loss account serves it for the Claude Code render, while HOME-009 serves it for the translation. Out of scope: Codex to Claude Code; adopting, wrapping or calling Codex's importer; Pi or any third harness; launching Codex through the launch template; Codex's thread index (state_5.sqlite, session_index.jsonl), which the render never writes; and any change to the Claude Code render or the importer.

requirements.title: Refuse an unmeasured Codex version, an unnamed or unknown time zone, an existing target and an unparsed stamp, each naming the act that answers it
requirements.spec: Add crates/lys-home/src/harness/codex/ (mod.rs holding only `pub mod` lines and `#[cfg(test)] mod` lines) and declare it in harness/mod.rs. In harness/codex/zone.rs define the measured version `0.156.0` and two checks. WHEN the Codex version given is not exactly `0.156.0`, THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse with HomeError::UnmeasuredCodexVersion, whose message is `Codex <version> has no measured rollout shape: render for 0.156.0 or card a measurement of the new version`. IF the zone given is absent, empty, or not an IANA-shaped name (one or more components of ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `+` and `-`, joined by single `/`, with no leading `/` or `:`), THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse with HomeError::UnnamedTimeZone, whose message is `TZ <value> is not an IANA time zone name: set TZ to an IANA name`, with `<value>` the word `unset` when absent. IF the zone is IANA-shaped and not in the time zone database, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse with HomeError::UnknownTimeZone, whose message is `time zone <zone> is not in the time zone database: set TZ to an IANA name`. The zone resolves through the jiff crate, added as a workspace dependency with its default features off and its tzdb-bundle-always feature on, so the time zone database is the one bundled in the build, the system time zone database is never read (the tzdb-zoneinfo, tzdb-concatenated, tzdb-bundle-platform and tz-system features stay off), and one zone name gives the same offsets on every machine. Add two variants for the translation's own refusals, beside LaunchTargetExists: HomeError::TranslationTargetExists, whose message is `translate-codex target already exists: <path>; choose another --out`, and HomeError::StampNotRfc3339, whose message is `entry <entry id> has a stamp that is not RFC 3339: re-import the source file`. This subcommand has no BlockNotStored refusal: the translation measures only what the home entry holds and reads no stored block, so no BlockNotStored variant is added and none is raised. HomeError::Exists, which import, canon, the Claude Code render, fewshot and the seed also raise, is left as it is; no existing variant's message changes. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT read an environment variable in harness/codex/, SHALL NOT fall back to UTC or the machine's zone, SHALL NOT accept a version by prefix, and SHALL NOT write any file before each check has passed.
acceptance: `cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::zone_tests::version_other_than_measured_is_refused` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; the test asserts the check of `0.157.0` displays exactly `Codex 0.157.0 has no measured rollout shape: render for 0.156.0 or card a measurement of the new version`, the check of `0.156` is refused with the same variant, and the check of `0.156.0` passes.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::zone_tests::unnamed_zone_is_refused` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; the test asserts an absent zone displays exactly `TZ unset is not an IANA time zone name: set TZ to an IANA name`, and that `` (empty) and `:/etc/localtime` are each refused as UnnamedTimeZone.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::zone_tests::unknown_zone_is_refused` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; the test asserts `Mars/Olympus` displays exactly `time zone Mars/Olympus is not in the time zone database: set TZ to an IANA name`.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::zone_tests::named_zone_resolves` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; the test asserts the instant `2000-01-02T03:04:05.678Z` in zone `Australia/Sydney` is local `2000-01-02T14:04:05`, and that `UTC` resolves.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::zone_tests::translation_refusals_name_the_act` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; the test asserts HomeError::TranslationTargetExists with path `a/b.jsonl` displays exactly `translate-codex target already exists: a/b.jsonl; choose another --out`, HomeError::StampNotRfc3339 with entry id `e1` displays exactly `entry e1 has a stamp that is not RFC 3339: re-import the source file`, and HomeError::Exists with path `a/b.jsonl` still displays exactly `session file already exists: a/b.jsonl`.
`grep -rn 'std::env' crates/lys-home/src/harness/codex/` prints nothing.
`grep -rn 'BlockNotStored' crates/lys-home/src` prints nothing.

`grep -nE '^jiff = ' Cargo.toml` prints one line, holding `default-features = false` and `tzdb-bundle-always`, and `cargo tree -p lys-home -e features -i jiff | grep -cE 'tzdb-zoneinfo|tzdb-concatenated|tzdb-bundle-platform|tz-system'` prints `0`.

requirements.title: Define the loss account: kept, changed and lost rows by entry id and hash, and nothing of the content
requirements.spec: In harness/codex/account.rs define the account written beside a rollout: a JSON object with exactly the keys `session` (the home session's id), `head` (the head entry's id), `head_hash` (Session::head_hash of the session at translation time, the source head hash the marker names), `thread` (the Codex thread id), `codex_version`, `kept`, `changed` and `lost`. A kept row has exactly `entry`, `hash`, `before` and `after`; a changed row has exactly `entry`, `hash`, `before`, `after` and `how`, where `how` names every field that was not carried or was reshaped, joined by `; `; a lost row has exactly `entry`, `hash`, `kind` and `reason`. `hash` is the block hash: the SHA-256, lowercase hex, of serde_json::to_vec of the part (or of the tool-result or other whole message) as the home entry holds it, the rule the Claude Code render's loss account uses, never a stored block, and is null for a row about an entry rather than a part. Rows are in walk order. The account measures the entry as the home holds it, so it cannot name a field the importer dropped before the entry was written: a tool_use's caller field is dropped at import and recorded nowhere yet, and the board 5 card "The importer records every field it drops" carries it. This account is S4's written account of what a translation lost. The account is written with create_new and synced before the translation reports. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT write into the account any text, argument, output, summary, note, epilogue or seed, only ids, hashes, kind names, field names and the fixed reason words this brief gives, and SHALL NOT count a part as kept when any of its fields was not carried or was reshaped.
acceptance: `cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::account_tests::account_holds_the_three_lists` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; the test builds an account with one row of each list and asserts its top-level keys are exactly `changed, codex_version, head, head_hash, kept, lost, session, thread`, a kept row's keys exactly `after, before, entry, hash`, a changed row's exactly `after, before, entry, hash, how`, a lost row's exactly `entry, hash, kind, reason`, and a row about an entry has `hash` null.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::account_tests::part_hash_is_the_entry_bytes` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; the test asserts the hash of the part `{"type":"text","text":"a"}` is `a7be9c132fa673d4eb9460cf2601c67404000175f92f2a576610aec68877d516` (computed independently by `printf '%s' '{"text":"a","type":"text"}' | shasum -a 256`).

Red first: the commit that adds this requirement's 2 named tests precedes the commit that adds its implementation, and at that commit `cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- harness::codex::account_tests` exits 101.

requirements.title: Carry each part whole as Codex's own item, thinking as text and base64 images as input_image, and count what changed
requirements.spec: In harness/codex/parts.rs map one message entry to Codex 0.156.0 response items and account rows. A user message's text parts, and string content, become one `message` item with role `user` and one `input_text` part per text, each text copied byte for byte; each is kept, before `text`, after `input_text`. An assistant message becomes items in part order: consecutive text and readable thinking parts form one `message` item with role `assistant` and one `output_text` part each; a toolCall part becomes one `function_call` item with `name`, `call_id` equal to the part's own id, and `arguments` equal to serde_json::to_string of the part's arguments, whole; a text part is kept, before `text`, after `output_text`; a toolCall is kept, before `toolCall`, after `function_call`. Every thinking part is treated as another provider's (the translation names no target model and the home's imported thinking is Anthropic's): readable thinking becomes an `output_text` part and is changed, before `thinking`, after `output_text`, with how `thinkingSignature not carried` when the part holds a signature and `thinking written as output_text` otherwise; redacted thinking is lost, reason `redacted thinking dropped: another provider`; thinking with no readable text is lost, reason `empty thinking dropped`. A toolResult entry becomes one `function_call_output` item with `call_id` equal to its toolCallId and `output` equal to its one text part's text as a string when its content is exactly one text part (how `content: one-item text array written as a string`), otherwise a list holding, in content order, `{"type":"input_text","text":…}` for each text part and the input_image item below for each base64 image part; it is one changed row keyed by the entry id and the hash of the toolResult message, before `toolResult`, after `function_call_output`, whose how also names `isError not carried`, `timestamp not carried` and `toolName not carried` for each of those keys the message holds. An image part (`{"type":"image","source":{…}}`, as the entry holds it in a user message or a tool result's content) whose source type is `base64` becomes `{"type":"input_image","image_url":"data:<media_type>;base64,<data>"}` with `<data>` copied byte for byte and no `detail` key, since the Claude session never held one (R11 measures that Codex 0.156.0 resumes a thread holding such an item, and if it does not, R11 adds the key as its conditional says), in its place among the message's parts or the output list, and is changed, before `image`, after `input_image`, how `source written as a data URL image_url`. An image part whose source type is anything else is left out and is a lost row with the part's hash, kind `image` and reason `image source <source type> not carried: part <index>, never fetched`, where `<index>` is the part's 0-based position in the content array that holds it; no byte of the source's value is written anywhere. A part of any other kind (an unknown assistant kind, a document) is lost, reason `Codex has no item for kind <kind> in this render`. A part holding a field beyond those its item carries (text: type, text; toolCall: type, id, name, arguments; thinking: type, thinking, thinkingSignature, redacted) is changed instead of kept, how naming `<field> not carried` for each. A home toolCall never holds a caller field, because the importer drops it; that loss is the board 5 card's to record and no test here asserts it. A toolCall whose `id` is absent, not a string or empty is left out and is a lost row with the part's hash, kind `toolCall` and reason `toolCall with no id: Codex's function_call needs a call_id`; one with an id and whose `name` is absent, not a string or empty is lost with reason `toolCall with no name: Codex's function_call needs a name`. A toolResult message whose `toolCallId` is absent, not a string or empty is left out and is one lost row keyed by the entry id and the hash of the message, kind `toolResult`, reason `toolResult with no toolCallId: Codex's function_call_output needs a call_id`. A message whose role is anything but user, assistant and toolResult is left out and is one lost row keyed by the entry id and the hash of the message, kind `<role> message`, or `message with no role` when it has no string role, and reason `Codex has no item for a message of this role`. Each user and assistant message entry whose message holds a key other than role and content gets one changed row with hash null, before `<role> message`, after `message item`, how naming `<key> not carried` for each such key in sorted order, so an assistant turn's model, usage and stop reason are named. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT clip or summarise any text, argument or output, SHALL NOT write an `[external_agent_tool_call` or `[external_agent_tool_result` note, SHALL NOT write a `custom_tool_call`, a `reasoning` item or `encrypted_content`, SHALL NOT write a thinking signature or redacted data into an item, and SHALL NOT write an `id` key on any item, SHALL NOT write a `detail` key on an input_image item, SHALL NOT fetch a URL or read any file to carry an image, and SHALL NOT put an empty string or any other default in place of a missing role, id, name or toolCallId.
acceptance: `cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::parts_tests::tool_call_becomes_function_call` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; a toolCall `{"type":"toolCall","id":"toolu_1","name":"Bash","arguments":{"command":"ls"}}` gives exactly `{"type":"function_call","name":"Bash","arguments":"{\"command\":\"ls\"}","call_id":"toolu_1"}` and one kept row before `toolCall`, after `function_call`.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::parts_tests::extra_part_field_is_changed` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; an assistant text part `{"type":"text","text":"a","textSignature":"s"}` gives an `output_text` part with text `a`, one changed row before `text`, after `output_text` with how exactly `textSignature not carried`, and no kept row.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::parts_tests::tool_call_without_id_or_name_is_lost` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; an assistant message whose parts are `{"type":"toolCall","id":"","name":"Bash","arguments":{}}` and `{"type":"toolCall","id":"toolu_2","arguments":{}}` gives no `function_call` item, exactly 2 lost rows of kind `toolCall` whose hashes are the two parts' hashes and whose reasons are exactly `toolCall with no id: Codex's function_call needs a call_id` and `toolCall with no name: Codex's function_call needs a name`, in that order.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::parts_tests::tool_result_without_call_id_is_lost` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; a toolResult message with toolCallId `` (empty) and content `[{"type":"text","text":"ok"}]` gives no item and exactly one lost row of kind `toolResult` whose hash is the message's hash and whose reason is exactly `toolResult with no toolCallId: Codex's function_call_output needs a call_id`; the same message with no toolCallId key gives the same row.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::parts_tests::unknown_role_is_lost` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; a message entry `m1` whose message is `{"role":"bashExecution","content":"x"}` gives no item and exactly one lost row with entry `m1`, the message's hash, kind exactly `bashExecution message` and reason exactly `Codex has no item for a message of this role`; a message with no role gives kind exactly `message with no role`.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::parts_tests::one_item_result_is_a_string` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; a toolResult message with toolCallId `toolu_1`, toolName `Bash`, content `[{"type":"text","text":"ok"}]`, isError false and timestamp 1 gives exactly `{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"toolu_1","output":"ok"}` and one changed row with how exactly `content: one-item text array written as a string; isError not carried; timestamp not carried; toolName not carried`.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::parts_tests::two_item_result_is_a_list` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; content with text parts `a` then `b` gives `output` exactly `[{"type":"input_text","text":"a"},{"type":"input_text","text":"b"}]`.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::parts_tests::assistant_turn_fields_are_named` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; an assistant message with keys role, content, api, provider, model, usage, stopReason and timestamp gives one row with hash null and how exactly `api not carried; model not carried; provider not carried; stopReason not carried; timestamp not carried; usage not carried`, and that row is in `changed`.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::parts_tests::thinking_is_text_and_opaque_is_lost` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; a thinking part with thinking `t` and thinkingSignature `sig` gives an `output_text` part with text `t` and a changed row with how `thinkingSignature not carried`; a redacted thinking part gives no item and a lost row whose hash is the part's hash and whose reason is exactly `redacted thinking dropped: another provider`; the serialised items contain neither `sig` nor `encrypted_content`.

`grep -rnE 'unwrap_or\(""\)|unwrap_or_default\(\)|unwrap_or_else\(String::new\)|String::new\(\)\)' crates/lys-home/src/harness/codex/` prints nothing.

requirements.title: Walk the context path and write the rollout at Codex's own layout, opening with the marker
requirements.spec: In harness/codex/rollout.rs define `translate`, the one entry point every later row extends and every test of R5 to R8 calls. WHEN a session is translated with an out directory, the Codex version and a zone, THE SYSTEM SHALL run R1's checks, then walk session.context_path() and write one rollout at `<out>/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SS-<thread>.jsonl` and its account at the same path with `.jsonl` replaced by `.loss.json`, where `<thread>` is record_uuid(session id, head entry id) and the date and time are the head entry's own stamp in the given zone, seconds truncated. IF either path exists, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse with HomeError::TranslationTargetExists naming it and write nothing. Every entry's stamp on the context path is parsed as RFC 3339 before any file is written; IF one does not parse, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse with HomeError::StampNotRfc3339 naming that entry's id, and write nothing. Every line is `{"timestamp","ordinal","type","payload"}` with `ordinal` the 0-based line number. Every line's outer `timestamp` is an entry's stamp copied character for character as that entry records it, never reformatted, re-precisioned or converted to the zone: lines 0 and 1 carry the head entry's stamp; each line of a message entry and the line of a compaction entry carry that entry's own stamp; a carried sidechain's developer line (R5) carries its `agent ` label entry's stamp; and a forked child's prompt line (R5) carries the stamp of the child's `lys.forked_from` entry.
